# transcdr_connection (Resource)

A connection: **storage** (`s3`, `gcs`, `azure_blob`, `ftp`, `ftps`, `sftp`, `http`, `webdav`) where inputs come from and outputs go, or **messaging** (`sqs`, `sns`, `webhook`) that receives events; an `sqs` connection can also trigger queue automations. Needs the Starter plan or above.

Transcdr tries the credentials when the connection is saved and records the outcome in `status` and `last_error`.

**Secrets are write-only.** The API never returns them, so Terraform keeps the values from your configuration. To rotate a credential, change its value here and apply. Removing a secret from the configuration clears it. The API does return a fingerprint of each secret that is set, which changes whenever the secret does: Terraform records it, and when a refresh finds a secret it set changed or cleared outside Terraform, it warns and the next plan sets the configured value again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An S3 bucket on AWS: where source files are read from and outputs written.
# Transcdr tests the credentials when the connection is saved; the result is
# in `status` ("ok" or "error") and `last_error`.
resource "transcdr_connection" "ingest" {
  name = "Ingest bucket"
  kind = "s3"
  config = {
    bucket = "media-in"
    region = "us-east-1"
    root   = "videos/" # optional: every path is relative to this folder
  }
  # Write-only: never returned by the API. Terraform keeps these values in
  # its state and sends them again only when they change; change them here
  # to rotate the credentials. Removing one clears it.
  secrets = {
    access_key_id     = aws_iam_access_key.transcdr.id
    secret_access_key = aws_iam_access_key.transcdr.secret
  }
}

# A Cloudflare R2 bucket: the S3 API with R2's endpoint and region "auto".
# Backblaze B2, Wasabi and MinIO work the same way with their own endpoint
# (MinIO also needs path_style = true).
resource "transcdr_connection" "r2" {
  name = "R2 media"
  kind = "s3"
  config = {
    bucket   = "media"
    region   = "auto"
    endpoint = "https://${var.cloudflare_account_id}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com"
  }
  secrets = {
    access_key_id     = var.r2_access_key_id
    secret_access_key = var.r2_secret_access_key
  }
}

# An SQS queue: a messaging connection that can trigger queue automations
# (and receive events). The region is read from the queue URL.
resource "transcdr_connection" "triggers" {
  name = "Upload events"
  kind = "sqs"
  config = {
    queue_url = aws_sqs_queue.triggers.url
  }
  secrets = {
    access_key_id     = aws_iam_access_key.transcdr.id
    secret_access_key = aws_iam_access_key.transcdr.secret
  }
}

# An SFTP server. Pinning the host key means a server presenting any other key
# is refused, instead of trusted on first use.
resource "transcdr_connection" "sftp" {
  name = "Studio SFTP"
  kind = "sftp"
  config = {
    host                 = "sftp.example.com"
    username             = "transcdr"
    root                 = "/exports"
    host_key_fingerprint = "SHA256:zE6s2Wf0gXJt0h9Q2mT7r8x1c4V5b6N7m8K9l0P1q2w"
  }
  secrets = {
    # Or password = "…"; an encrypted key also needs private_key_passphrase.
    private_key = file("${path.module}/transcdr_ed25519")
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `config` (Attributes) Non-secret settings. Which fields apply depends on `kind`:

| kind | config |
|---|---|
| `s3` (AWS, R2, B2, Wasabi, MinIO…) | `bucket`, `region`, `endpoint`, `path_style`, `root` |
| `gcs` | `bucket`, `root` |
| `azure_blob` | `account`, `bucket` (the container), `root` |
| `ftp` / `ftps` | `host`, `port`, `username`, `root`, `passive` |
| `sftp` | `host`, `port`, `username`, `root`, `host_key_fingerprint` |
| `http` (read-only) | `endpoint`, `username` |
| `webdav` | `endpoint`, `username`, `root` |
| `sqs` | `queue_url`, `region`, `message_group_id` |
| `sns` | `topic_arn`, `region`, `endpoint`, `message_group_id` |
| `webhook` | `url` |

Updates merge into the stored config; a field removed here is cleared. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config))
- `kind` (String) One of `s3`, `gcs`, `azure_blob`, `ftp`, `ftps`, `sftp`, `http`, `webdav` (storage) or `sqs`, `sns`, `webhook` (messaging). Changing it replaces the connection.
- `name` (String) A name, up to 120 characters.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the connection is on. Transcdr turns a connection off by itself after a permanent failure (or 5 transient ones in a row); the next plan then shows `enabled` going back to `true`, and applying it tests the connection again and turns it back on. Default true.
- `secrets` (Attributes, Sensitive) Write-only credentials:

| kind | secrets |
|---|---|
| `s3` | `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, `session_token` |
| `gcs` | `service_account_json` |
| `azure_blob` | `account_key` or `sas_token` |
| `ftp` / `ftps` | `password` |
| `sftp` | `password` or `private_key` (+ `private_key_passphrase`) |
| `http` | `password` (basic, with `config.username`) or `bearer_token` |
| `webdav` | `password` or `bearer_token` |
| `sqs` / `sns` | `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key` |
| `webhook` | none: events are signed with the event destination's secret |

Never read back from the API: see the note above on rotation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secrets))

### Read-Only

- `capabilities` (Attributes) What the connection can be used for. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--capabilities))
- `class` (String) `storage` or `messaging`.
- `disabled_reason` (String) Why the connection was turned off: `<activity>: <error>`, or `Disabled by hand.`.
- `failure_count` (Number) Transient failures in a row; any success resets it.
- `id` (String) The connection id, `con_…`.
- `last_error` (String) The last test's error, if it failed.
- `secrets_set` (Set of String) The names of the secrets that are stored. Their values are never returned.
- `status` (String) The last test's outcome: `untested`, `ok` or `error`.

<a id="nestedatt--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config`

Optional:

- `account` (String) `azure_blob`: the storage account name.
- `bucket` (String) `s3`/`gcs`: the bucket. `azure_blob`: the container.
- `endpoint` (String) `s3`: a custom endpoint (R2, B2, Wasabi, MinIO…); omit for AWS. `http`/`webdav`: the base URL. `sns`: an SNS-compatible service endpoint instead of AWS's.
- `host` (String) `ftp`/`ftps`/`sftp`: the host name.
- `host_key_fingerprint` (String) `sftp`: the expected host key, `SHA256:…`. Any other key is refused.
- `message_group_id` (String) `sqs`/`sns`: the message group of FIFO queues and topics receiving events.
- `passive` (Boolean) `ftp`/`ftps`: passive mode (the API's default is true).
- `path_style` (Boolean) `s3`: address the bucket by path rather than by subdomain (MinIO, LocalStack). Default false.
- `port` (Number) `ftp`/`ftps`/`sftp`: the port, when not the protocol's default.
- `queue_url` (String) `sqs`: the queue URL, e.g. `https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/transcdr`.
- `region` (String) `s3`: the bucket's region (`auto` for R2). `sqs`/`sns`: read from the queue URL or topic ARN when omitted; required when it cannot be (e.g. a non-AWS queue URL).
- `root` (String) Every path is relative to this folder inside the connection, e.g. `videos/`.
- `topic_arn` (String) `sns`: the topic ARN.
- `url` (String) `webhook`: the https URL events are POSTed to.
- `username` (String) `ftp`/`ftps`/`sftp`/`webdav`: the login name; `http`: the basic-auth user name.


<a id="nestedatt--secrets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secrets`

Optional:

- `access_key_id` (String, Sensitive) `s3`, `sqs`, `sns`: the access key ID.
- `account_key` (String, Sensitive) `azure_blob`: the account key (or use `sas_token`).
- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive) `http`/`webdav`: sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) `ftp`/`ftps`/`sftp`/`webdav`, and `http` basic auth (with `config.username`).
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) `sftp`: a private key (OpenSSH or PEM).
- `private_key_passphrase` (String, Sensitive) `sftp`: the private key's passphrase.
- `sas_token` (String, Sensitive) `azure_blob`: a SAS token.
- `secret_access_key` (String, Sensitive) `s3`, `sqs`, `sns`: the secret access key.
- `service_account_json` (String, Sensitive) `gcs`: a service account JSON key.
- `session_token` (String, Sensitive) `s3`: a session token, for temporary credentials.


<a id="nestedatt--capabilities"></a>
### Nested Schema for `capabilities`

Read-Only:

- `destination` (Boolean) Outputs can be delivered to it.
- `events` (Boolean) It can receive events (messaging kinds).
- `source` (Boolean) Inputs can be read from it.
- `trigger` (Boolean) It can trigger `queue` automations (`sqs`).
- `watch` (Boolean) It can be listed, so a `watch` automation can poll it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A connection id, con_...
terraform import transcdr_connection.ingest con_4Qm8x2Lk9Pz7Rt5Vw3Yb1N
```
